workspace-bound-agent-grant-01.graded_text: Each agent connection is bound to one firm workspace chosen at consent and approved by that firm's Admin, and a consultant who works for several firms makes a separate connection for each.

votes.e: B/project/docs/agent-access.md:12: "Each MCP connection is authorized for exactly one firm workspace. The consultant picks that workspace when they consent ... every tool call is refused until an Admin of that firm approves the grant ... A consultant who works for three firms has three separate grants, each approved by its own firm's Admin." Reinforced by :17 "Choosing a different firm means a new authorization of the same resource, which produces a new token bound to that other firm", :60 "One grant per (workspace, consultant, client)", and approval flow :67 "On consent they pick one firm" / :70 "An Admin opens Settings → Agent connections in that firm's workspace ... They approve ... or deny it".

workspace-bound-agent-grant-02.graded_text: The server checks on every call that the target belongs to the connection's bound workspace and that the consultant's membership and role are still live, so removal from a firm cuts off an existing connection.

votes.e: B/project/docs/agent-access.md gate, every tool call: :81 "3. Confirm the consultant is a current member of that workspace and look up their role.", :82 "4. Load the grant for (workspace, subject, client) and require `approved`.", :84 "6. Run the product operation scoped to that workspace. Every query is filtered by `workspaceId` inside the operation itself, not only checked beforehand.", :86 "A workpaper ID that belongs to another firm returns the same \"not found\" as an ID that doesn't exist." Removal cuts existing connections: :63 "Role and membership are read live from the provider-backed membership at every call, so removing someone from a firm, or changing their role, takes effect on the next call with no sync job."

workspace-bound-agent-grant-03.graded_text: The design offers no connection whose scope spans more than one firm.
